Title: "Pump Module Selection for the Water-Reclamation Transfer Loop (WO-01)"

Executive summary (~110 words): Four candidate pump modules were evaluated for the water-reclamation transfer loop under the client's qualification policy: quality index at least 80 and raw defect count at most 5, then lowest measured energy on a common acceptance run. All four candidates qualify on both gates. Measured energies range from 12 to 58 kWh. P2 dominates on the decision metric at 12 kWh — 40 kWh (69%) below the next-lowest qualifier P3 — while carrying the highest quality index (97) and a single raw defect. No cost, delivery or field-reliability data was supplied, so ranking rests solely on the supplied quality, defect and energy records. Recommendation: select P2.

Sections:
1. Qualification screening (eligibility gates)
2. Energy comparison and gaps
3. Data limitations and open questions
4. Risk review / recommendation rationale... must have exactly four substantive sections plus recommendation object. Maybe sections: 1) Qualification screening; 2) Energy ranking and gaps; 3) Quality–defect trade-offs; 4) Open questions and verification needs.

Section 1 (Qualification screening): "All four candidates clear both policy gates. Quality indices are P1 84, P2 97, P3 80, P4 81 — every value meets the minimum of 80, with P3 sitting exactly at the threshold. Raw defect counts are P1 4, P2 1, P3 3, P4 0 — all within the maximum of 5, and P4 reports none. No candidate is eliminated, so the ranking decision falls entirely to the energy criterion. Note that P3's exact-threshold quality leaves zero tolerance for any future measurement revision; a one-point drop would disqualify it." ~90 words.

Section 2 (Energy ranking): "Measured energy on the shared acceptance run: P2 12 kWh, P3 52, P1 56, P4 58. P2 leads by 40 kWh over P3 (a 77% reduction relative to P3, or 69% below the qualifier average of ~47.5). Gaps among the three slower modules are small: P3 to P1 is 4 kWh, P1 to P4 is 2 kWh, so these three are nearly interchangeable on energy, whereas P2 is a clear outlier. Under the policy's minimize-energy rule, P2 is the unambiguous qualifying winner regardless of how the remaining ties would resolve." ~90 words. Compute qualifier average: (56+12+52+58)/4 = 178/4 = 44.5. Use 44.5. 12 vs 44.5: 73% below. Let me say "well below the qualifier average of 44.5 kWh".

Section 3 (Quality–defect trade-offs): "P2 pairs the lowest energy with the strongest quality index (97) and one recorded defect, so no trade-off sacrifices quality to obtain the energy saving. P4 offers a zero-defect record but the highest energy (58 kWh, 46 kWh above P2). P1 and P3 carry more defects (4 and 3) and higher energy; P3's threshold quality adds fragility. If the client valued defect-free build alone, P4 would be a candidate, but the stated policy makes energy the deciding metric once gates pass, and P4 trails P2 by 46 kWh." ~80 words.

Section 4 (Open questions): "Several inputs were not supplied and remain unverified: unit cost, delivery schedule, maintenance burden, and field reliability beyond the acceptance run. The single energy measurement per candidate also cannot reveal variability or degradation. Cost-per-kWh comparisons, spares strategy and vendor responsiveness therefore cannot be ranked from this record. Before final procurement, request costed quotes and reliability history for P2 and the runner-up P3, and confirm the acceptance-run duty matches the actual transfer-loop duty. None of these questions changes the ranking under the supplied policy." ~80 words.

Recommendation: P2, rationale ≤350: "P2 is the lowest-energy qualifying candidate at 12 kWh, 40 kWh below runner-up P3, while also holding the highest quality index (97) and only one defect. All four candidates pass both policy gates, so energy decides; P2 leads by a margin far larger than any measurement nuance supplied. Limitations: cost, delivery and field data are absent; the ranking is one acceptance run deep. Select P2, and procure verification quotes for P3 as fallback." ~65 words.

Caption: "Job illustration: energy comparison of the four qualified pump modules on the common acceptance run, with P2 selected." ~110 chars.
